31982102.extract:
# 1982 Los Angeles Rams–Green Bay Packers Game

The **1982 Los Angeles Rams–Green Bay Packers game** was an American football game played on September 12, 1982, at Milwaukee County Stadium in Milwaukee, Wisconsin, between the Los Angeles Rams and the Green Bay Packers during Week 1 of the 1982 NFL season. The game was notable for a dramatic 23-point second-half comeback by the Packers, who won 35–23.

The Rams dominated the first half, scoring 23 points while shutting out the Packers, who committed five turnovers. However, the Packers staged a complete reversal in the second half, with quarterback Lynn Dickey leading five consecutive scoring drives. The Packers defense held the Rams scoreless in the second half and limited them to four first downs. The 23-point comeback tied the Packers' team record for the largest comeback, a record that would remain tied for 31 years until the 2013 Packers–Cowboys game.

# Background

The 1982 season began under unusual circumstances. In late September, the NFL Players Association initiated a 57-day strike that reduced the regular season from 16 games to 9 games. The two teams entered Week 1 with vastly different recent histories. The Rams, after eight consecutive seasons of playoff appearances, had missed the playoffs for the first time in 1981, compiling a 6–10 record. Under head coach Ray Malavasi, the Rams were attempting to return to contention.

The Packers, meanwhile, had not appeared in the playoffs since 1972 and had not won a playoff game since 1967. Head coach Bart Starr, the legendary quarterback of the Packers' 1960s dynasty, had accumulated a disappointing record of 39–65–2 through his first seven seasons in charge. In 1981, the Packers finished 8–8 but missed the playoffs by losing their final game to the New York Jets, 28–3.

Because of the players strike, the Packers played their first home game of the season at Milwaukee County Stadium rather than at Lambeau Field. This would be Green Bay's season opener, while the Rams were in their second week of play.

# Game Summary

### First Half

The Rams struck quickly in the first quarter. Running back Wendell Tyler scored on a 4-yard touchdown run, and kicker Mike Lansford added a 32-yard field goal to give Los Angeles a 10–0 lead. In the second quarter, Rams quarterback Bert Jones connected with tight end Mike Barber on an 8-yard touchdown pass, extending the lead to 17–0. Lansford then kicked two field goals of 29 and 28 yards, giving the Rams a commanding 23–0 halftime lead.

The Packers' offensive struggles in the first half were compounded by turnovers. The defense allowed Jones to complete 17 of 31 passes for 202 yards, although Jones was sacked four times for 36 yards total loss. By halftime, the Rams had dominated the line of scrimmage and the statistical categories. The Packers appeared outmatched and headed toward a season-opening defeat.

### Second Half

The second half witnessed a dramatic reversal of fortune. Early in the third quarter, Packers quarterback Lynn Dickey led a 55-yard drive that resulted in a 4-yard touchdown pass to tight end Paul Coffman, cutting the deficit to 23–7. Minutes later, running back Eddie Lee Ivery scored on a 3-yard run, narrowing the gap to 23–14.

The momentum had shifted entirely to Green Bay. The Packers defense, which had been relatively quiet in the first half, tightened considerably. The Rams could generate no offensive rhythm, and the Packers forced three interceptions while recovering a fumble. Bert Jones was intercepted multiple times, including picks by Randy Perry, Nolan Cromwell, and Carl Ekern.

In the fourth quarter, Dickey continued his assault. Wide receiver James Lofton caught a 15-yard touchdown pass to make the score 23–21. Coffman then caught his second touchdown of the game, a 10-yard reception that gave the Packers a 28–23 lead. With the game still in doubt, Ivery capped the Packers' remarkable comeback with a 27-yard touchdown run, securing the 35–23 victory.

Dickey finished the game with 17 completions on 27 attempts for 237 yards and three touchdown passes, along with three interceptions. His passer rating of 88.6 was substantially higher than that of Jones, who posted a 58.8 rating. Ivery led the Packers' rushing attack with 109 yards on 17 carries and two touchdowns. The Packers totaled 377 yards of offense compared to the Rams' 271 yards.

# Significance

The game marked the beginning of an unlikely resurgence for the Packers. Though they finished the strike-shortened 1982 season with a 5–3–1 record, the team made their first playoff appearance in ten years. Dickey's performance in this game set the tone for his leadership of the team throughout the season. The Packers defeated the St. Louis Cardinals 41–16 in the first playoff game at Lambeau Field since 1967, although they subsequently lost to the Dallas Cowboys 37–26 in the divisional round.

The 23-point comeback remained the Packers' largest comeback from any deficit for over three decades. The franchise record was tied on December 15, 2013, when backup quarterback Matt Flynn led the Packers to a 37–36 victory over the Dallas Cowboys after the team fell behind 26–3 at halftime.

Historically, the game has been mentioned as one of the most significant contests in the rivalry between the Rams and Packers franchises.
